terminal_record.title: CNP Membership Compilations Have Different Scopes
terminal_record.description_short: Supplied material describes two incomplete CNP membership compilations but does not establish Donald Trump’s membership or role.
terminal_record.description_medium: Supplied material describes one Council for National Policy compilation as listing 1,011 names from 1981–2020 while covering fewer than half of its members, and a separate 2020 directory said to contain 426 names. The different lists are not a combined membership count. The material does not establish Donald Trump’s membership or any Trump action, so this remains an unverified CNP-history draft.
terminal_record.description_long: Supplied material describes two Council for National Policy membership compilations. It says a TrumpFile compilation spans 1981 to 2020 and lists 1,011 names; its compiler reportedly cautions that it covers fewer than half of the council’s members. A separate directory, described as leaked in September 2020, is said to list 426 people. These figures refer to different documents and should not be added or treated as a total membership count. The frozen entry’s January 20, 1981 date does not establish when either list was created or released. The supplied materials do not confirm Donald Trump’s membership, attendance, participation, or a policy action connected to CNP. This draft therefore describes only the supplied list-scope claims and does not assert a Trump-related event. The counts and dates remain unverified, and a dated membership or participation source, or an explicit scope decision to treat this as CNP history, is needed to resolve the hold.

terminal_record.title: Supplied Allegation of Deutsche Bank Lending to Trump Projects
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied account alleges long-running Deutsche Bank lending to Trump; its $640 million aggregate remains unverified.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied account alleges that Deutsche Bank financed Trump projects through its private-wealth division, describing more than $640 million in lending from the late 1990s through the 2000s. A supplied note says this figure may combine a Chicago construction loan with later lending, rather than represent a verified portfolio total. The claims remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_long: According to the supplied entry, Deutsche Bank maintained a lending relationship with Donald Trump beginning in the late 1990s and extending into the 2000s. The account says the bank’s private-wealth division financed Trump National Doral and hotels in Chicago and Las Vegas despite earlier casino bankruptcies and defaults. It gives an aggregate above $640 million, but the supplied research note warns that the figure may combine a Chicago construction loan with later private-wealth loans rather than represent one verified portfolio total. The record also says congressional Democrats subpoenaed bank records during Trump's presidency and that the information was not made public; no specific subpoena or release history is established in this draft. It alleges the lending created financial leverage that foreign intelligence services could exploit, a concern rather than a demonstrated consequence. The packet does not settle loan amounts, dates, divisions, or project allocations. All these details remain allegations or uncertain figures from the supplied record; no motive or wrongdoing is established. This internal draft is not publication-eligible.
